Amulet bowl formula for exorcising broken or malfunctioning electrical appliances

tei:div.tei:head: Amulet bowl formula for exorcising broken or malfunctioning electrical appliances

tei:lg.tei:l: of [name] son / daughter / house of [father’s name]
Sealed and signed with the signet of YQWQ of Hosts,
this hidden secret is one secret and one decree
that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Peraḥya decreed against you.
You have received the ban that you will be banned,
and ye will be in the ban of Rabbi Yehoshua bar Peraḥya,
and you will be in the ban in the name of Asmodeus king of demons,
and you will be in the ban in the name of Hormiz son of Lilith,
and you will be in the ban in the name of Rav Yosef the Demon,
and you will be in the ban in the name of Shivta,
and you will be in the ban in the name of Mishavriri Shavriri Briri Riri Iri Ri,
and you will be in the ban of all demons and darknesses, lilin and liliths,
that are in the land of Israel and that are in Babylonia.
pulled, bound with binding, chained with chain,
with the signet of YWKBR ZYWʾ MṢPṢ HŠTPʾ ʾKTRYʾL
from demons and daevas and lilin all.
for [name] son / daughter / house of [father’s name] —
from their blood I take for sealing them,
and from their skin I take for patching them,

tei:note.tei:p: Literally: sons, but in the plural used to refer to all children

The word for “telephone” here, רְחִיקָּל, is an original coinage, combining רְחִיק far and קָל sound, as a calque of telephone (literally: far-sound). The words for washer, computer, and AC are adapted from modern Hebrew, since they are all in forms with Aramaic parallels. Ovens existed in ancient Babylon too so I just usted the same word for that one.
Referred to as such in Pesachim 110a and Gittin 68a, this demon is first mentioned in the book of Tobit, and probably derives from the Avestan phrase aēšma-daēva = wrath-demon.

See Bava Batra 73a:11. The name “Hormiz” probably derives from the Zoroastrian deity Ahura Mazda. This deity is, in Zoroastrian contet, seen as a good deity. Some texts of the Gemara read “Hormin,” which may derive from the Zoroastrian evil deity Ahriman. Lilith is in this context simply the primordial mother-demon.

See Pesachim 110a and Eruvin 43a. Yosef the Demon, who used his mystical powers to go from study hall to study hall, is not referred to as a rabbi in the Gemara but is so in the magic bowl literature, perhaps on account of being mixed up with the human Rav Yosef.
See Taanit 20b, Yoma 77b, and Chullin 107b. Shivta is the demon that infests unwashed hands.

See Pesachim 112a and Avodah Zarah 12b. Mishavriri Shavriri Briri Riri Iri Ri, also known as Shavriri for short, is the demon of blindness. This is the source of the video game Elden Ring’s “Shabriri.”
Here a synecdoche for the diaspora as a whole.
A common divine name in the magic bowl literature.
